overall: Washington DC hit its daily maximum of 96.8°F at approximately 15:04 ET, and as of 19:45 ET — nearly 5 hours post-peak — temperatures have pulled back to 95.0°F and are cooling at -1.8°F/hr (with the 30-minute velocity even steeper at -3.1°F/hr). The running max has been flatlined at 96.8°F since ~16:52 ET, confirming the day's high is locked in. An Extreme Heat Warning remains in effect through July 3, though the worst heat for this event is forecast for Thursday and Friday.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models were broadly too warm for today: GFS (101.4°F) and ECMWF (99.1°F) overshot significantly, while HRRR (96.9°F) came closest to the observed 96.8°F peak and NBM (97.9°F) was the next best. The peak also arrived earlier than the model-mean timing of 15:00h suggested, and the combination of an afternoon cloud fraction increase (FEW at 12%) and a modest wind shift may have capped the afternoon high below the upper-model guidance.
max_temp_prediction: With the peak definitively in at 96.8°F and a firm cooling trend underway nearly 5 hours after the high, today's TMAX is effectively certain at 96.8°F. This lands squarely in the 96–97°F even bucket. The intraday model assigns ~27% probability to the 96–97°F bucket (its second-highest), which is consistent with current observations now that higher outcomes are foreclosed. Confidence is extremely high — approaching certainty — that the final TMAX will be reported as 96.8°F (96°F–97°F range).
